summary: A 1945 fire lookout beside the Klamath Falls Marine treatment barracks (1944-46); the Forest Lookouts page lists the tower as removed.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed; no source describes what remains at the site.

access.note: The North Ridge Marine Corps Memorial is a small park with information panels; no source describes the former tower site.

events.note: Marine treatment barracks at Klamath Falls; first Marines arrive in April 1944
New fire lookout built near the barracks, per a caption dated August 6, 1945
Three men on duty around the clock, manned by men from the installation
Lookout no longer used after the barracks closed
Marine Barracks Memorial Park created on Old Fort Road
Memorial park moved a short distance and renamed North Ridge Marine Corps Memorial

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 2016 radio history places a granite headstone at the end of Old Fort Road marking the park; the Herald and News says the park was relocated and renamed in 2019. Both are accurate for their dates.

sources.title: Klamath Falls Marine Barracks Treats Tropical Diseases

notes_for_editor: Tower facts rest on one Forest Lookouts page that quotes 1944-45 Herald and News items. Two searches found no second source placing the tower, its design or its removal date. The status 'Removed' is the page's own word. The memorial history comes from a 2016 radio piece and a Herald and News article; they differ only by date. The access level 'public' is inferred from the memorial park with panels, not from a statement about the tower site.
